headline: Mark Todd warns Fed's 'Operation Twist' risks credibility as it buys back bonds weeks after issuing at 2007 highs
reasoning: Todd draws a comparison between the Fed's current 'twist' operation and the original 1961 Kennedy-era twist, arguing the Fed of 2026 has far less credibility. He notes the Fed issued at 2007 highs just two weeks prior and is now buying back double what it previously flagged, calling this incoherent fiscal behaviour. He highlights that 10x oversubscription at the start of the week signals a problem in the Treasury market. The Fed's desired outcome is to push rates lower to avoid heavy coupon payments (e.g. $85bn in one week), but its options — raising taxes, cutting spending — conflict with the administration's ideological commitments. Todd suggests belief systems may override pragmatism, making fiscal consolidation difficult.
quote: So if you if you are running surpluses, you could buy back your debt. That sort of makes sense... Now you've got something like the fed where they're saying basically we're going to borrow short to invest long, and we've changed our mind in the space of two weeks, having just issued at 2007 highs, we're now buying them back. It's just if it was a, um, Katie would call it a banana republic, they would just say that that just doesn't make any sense. First you've just borrowed, now you've gone and bought them back and you're going to buy double what you said you'd buy two weeks previously. And so when you put your hand up at the start of the week and say, look, I want 2 billion and it's ten times oversubscribed, you know, there's a problem in Paradise.
